comment: Edits on fetched sources, each must match exactly once. tree: ath12k (drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k) or freebsd (repository root). Edited FreeBSD headers go to an overlay searched first. LinuxKPI edits lx-device-of-node, lx-bss-conf-fields, lx-reg-rule-psd, lx-channel-psd and lx-regd-sync-copies are adapted from hackios wifi/lx/patches (MIT), see xnu/fuxi-ath12k/compat/PROVENANCE.md.

edits.why: ath12k reads dev->of_node; here it stays NULL.
LinuxKPI bug: size_mul() is given one argument, so kmalloc_objs() cannot compile; kzalloc_objs() has it right.
edits.replace: kmalloc(size_mul((_n), sizeof(typeof(_p))), default_gfp(__VA_ARGS__))

edits.why: mac.c reads the MBSSID transmitter, the AP power constraint and two EHT flags of a link.
mac.c copies the station's EML capabilities; stays 0 without MLO.
edits.replace:
uint16_t				eml_cap;
	struct ieee80211_link_sta		deflink;

edits.why: mac.c sets this flag when the chip can do MLO, which it does not here.
edits.replace:
IEEE80211_HW_NO_VIRTUAL_MONITOR,
	IEEE80211_HW_MLO_MCAST_MULTI_LINK_TX,

edits.why: Linux 7.0 reports statistics per link; ath12k's op table fills this member, which LinuxKPI does not have.
edits.find: void (*sta_statistics)(struct ieee80211_hw *, struct ieee80211_vif *, struct ieee80211_sta *, struct station_info *);
edits.replace:
void (*sta_statistics)(struct ieee80211_hw *, struct ieee80211_vif *, struct ieee80211_sta *, struct station_info *);
	void (*link_sta_statistics)(struct ieee80211_hw *, struct ieee80211_vif *, struct ieee80211_link_sta *, struct link_station_info *);

edits.why: The members of Linux 7.0's per-link statistics that mac.c fills.
reg.c fills the power spectral density of a rule.
mac.c reads the power spectral density of a channel.
edits.replace:
struct linuxkpi_ieee80211_channel {
	int8_t					psd;	/* power spectral density, dBm/MHz */

edits.why: LinuxKPI's inline keeps the caller's pointer and refuses unless self-managed; ath12k frees its copy, so the domain must be copied as Linux does.
edits.replace:
/* (the caller keeps and may free regd: a copy is made, as Linux makes one) */
	return (linuxkpi_regulatory_set_wiphy_regd_sync(wiphy, regd));

edits.why: wifi7/dp_tx.c fills the EHT resource unit of a rate.
wifi7/hw.c recognizes ADDBA responses. Layout per 802.11-2024 9.6.4.3.
802.11-2020 Table 9-359: ADDBA Response is 1.
edits.replace:
WLAN_ACTION_ADDBA_REQ		= 0,
	WLAN_ACTION_ADDBA_RESP		= 1,

edits.why: 802.11-2020 Table 9-92: Nontransmitted BSSID Capability is element 83.
edits.replace:
enum ieee80211_eid {
	WLAN_EID_NON_TX_BSSID_CAP		= 83,

edits.why: %pV is a Linux printk extension that XNU's printf does not have; each message would print a pointer.
edits.replace: lx_vlog(fmt, args);

edits.why: As above.
edits.replace: lx_vlog(fmt, args);

edits.why: As above; keeps the rate limit.
edits.replace: lx_vlog_ratelimited(fmt, args);

edits.why: As above.
edits.replace: lx_vlog(fmt, args);

edits.why: Design R3: fuxi's wiring is unknown and a wrongly reported switch disables the radio with no error. 48 is WCN7850's; with 0 ath12k_mac_rfkill_config() declines. fa_hif.c logs that this edit is in force.
edits.replace:
.rfkill_pin = 0,	/* fuxi: design R3 */
		.rfkill_cfg = 0,
		.rfkill_on_level = 1,

edits.why: Design section 3: REO queue descriptors must be memory the radio can reach, so they come from pool rings instead of kzalloc().
edits.replace: vaddr = lx_dma_zalloc(hw_desc_sz + HAL_LINK_DESC_ALIGN - 1);

edits.why: The failure path of that allocation.
edits.replace:
lx_dma_free(vaddr, hw_desc_sz + HAL_LINK_DESC_ALIGN - 1);
			return ret;

edits.why: Its normal free; the same size as the allocation.
edits.replace: lx_dma_free(tid_qbuf->vaddr, tid_qbuf->size + HAL_LINK_DESC_ALIGN - 1);

edits.why: Design R6: returning before the replenish loses buffers whose MSDUs were all dropped. The early return moves after the loop (with -b).
edits.replace:
for (device_id = 0; device_id < ATH12K_MAX_DEVICES; device_id++) {
		if (!num_buffs_reaped[device_id])

edits.why: See ath12k-rx-refill-guard-a.
Design section 4: the address given to iOS at attach, before the radio exists, must be the radio's; mac.c has no device-address fallback.
LinuxKPI's cfg80211_find_ie() answers NULL always with a TODO; mac.c's beacon parsing needs the element. Same walk as cfg80211_find_elem() beside it.
There is no mesh here, so false is the true answer. dp_tx.c asks for each frame: with TODO() logging on (fa_80211.c) this would flood the log.
LinuxKPI refuses silently (SKB_TODO is compiled out). Buffers cannot grow here; the failure is ath12k's to handle but must show in the log.
As lx-pskb-expand-says. Design section 4 keeps hw->extra_tx_headroom free so TX should not get here.
Design M1: stop after HTC ready through ath12k_core_start's normal error path.

Design M2: stop once the radio is registered, with WMI ready and hw_mode behind it, before the data rings are set up. What ath12k_mac_register() did is undone, then the error path below it and the caller's ath12k_core_stop() run.
Design M2: upstream error lines must be absent when the stage stops as planned. Any other failure still says it.
edits.replace:
if (ret != -ECANCELED)
				ath12k_warn(ab, "unable to start hw group\n");

edits.why: Design section 9: LinuxKPI's IEEE80211_EHT_PHY_CAP* and PPE threshold values are running counters, so this function would filter the wrong bits and offer the result. eht_cap stays zero, has_eht false. linuxkpi_80211_wiphy_register() refuses a radio that offers it.

Design M2: WMI_INIT and service_ready_ext on this CNSS-class image are unknown offline, and a silent firmware leaves only a timeout. The boot shows which events came, in order. Says only the first ones.
